subject: LLM execution locations, subprocessors, and erase (tombstone) commitments - Cedar Health Q&A
messages:
From: Emma Larson <emma@cedarhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Qs on where requests run + deletion window

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we proceed to procurement I have a couple of technical/regulatory questions from our security team:

1) For API calls to your hosted service, can you provide a concise mapping of where requests are executed (region/hop level)? We need to know if any processing or caching happens outside the US for US-resident data.

2) Who are the subprocessors involved in the execution path (including cloud infra, networking, caching layers)?

3) On deletion: if we invoke a customer-initiated deletion request (or a user data erasure), what is the expected timeline for data to be irrecoverably removed from all runtime caches and backups (we call this the \"tombstone\" commitment)? Our legal/infosec folks prefer measured SLOs.

Appreciate anything concise you can share — we don’t need low-level logs yet, just architecture, list of subprocessors, and pragmatic timelines.

Best,
Emma
Emma Larson
Senior Security Engineer
Cedar Health

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests run + deletion window

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Below is an overview we typically share with prospects; I’ve attached a concise execution map and our SOC 2 summary for reference. If you need a deeper packet (subprocessor contracts, network traces), we can escalate to an evidence request.

1) Execution locations (short):
- Primary execution for Cedar Health workloads can be pinned to US regions (us-west-2 / us-east-1) by contract.
- By default, requests land on the nearest Redwood edge for ingress, then are routed to a pinned runtime pool. No inference computation occurs outside the runtime pool selected for the tenant.
- Transient hops (load balancers, edge proxies) may be in other RDNS regions for routing optimization but do not persist payloads beyond short-lived caches (<120s) unless caching is explicitly enabled.

2) Subprocessors (execution path):
- Cloud infra: AWS (EC2/GPU instances), S3 for model artifact storage.
- Networking/edge: Fastly (edge proxy), internal routing fabric (Redwood-managed).
- Observability/telemetry: Datadog (traces/metrics), but sensitive payloads are redacted in traces by default.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS integrations are supported; Redwood KMS is optional.

3) Deletion (tombstone) commitments — practical SLOs:
- Runtime cache eviction: immediate on request (within seconds), KV/prefix caches are invalidated on tombstone call.
- Persistent logs/metrics: aggregated telemetry (non-PHI) retained per our policy; request-level logs containing payloads are deleted within 72 hours by default for hosted customers who do not opt in to extended retention.
- Backups and long-term storage: model artifacts unaffected; customer payload snapshots used for debugging are retained only with explicit consent; standard hosted backup tombstone window is 30 days for queued retention artifacts, 90 days maximum for archived evidence unless otherwise contracted (Dedicated/Private customers can negotiate shorter windows).

Attachments: redwood_execution_map_v1.pdf (high-level hop map), soc2-type2-summary.pdf

If it helps, we can create a short mutual action plan and a targeted evidence bundle for procurement to review.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben for any follow-ups on subnet-level evidence.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Ben / Evelyn — confirmed for pin to us-west-2:
- Infra subprocessors: AWS (EC2/GPU runtimes), EBS for ephemeral instance storage.
- Edge: Fastly (ingress POPs), but no persisted payloads in Fastly.
- Caching: Redwood managed Redis clusters (ephemeral, flushed on tombstone).
- Observability: Datadog traces redact payloads; request IDs only retained for 30 days for troubleshooting by default.

Evidence we can include in the pack: flow diagrams, TTL logs showing cache evictions, S3 lifecycle rules for backup removal. I’ll drop the TTL snippets into the evidence Drive folder by EOD.

Emma — thanks for your patience. Attaching the execution map and a short erase playbook (outline) we discussed. High level summary for your pack and legal:

- Execution locality: Redwood routes ingress to edge POPs; inference computation and KV caches are executed in the pinned runtime pool (we can contractually pin to US regions). Transient routing does not persist payloads beyond short caches.
- Subprocessors: AWS, Fastly (edge), Datadog (telemetry). We maintain subprocessors roster and can provide a redacted contract summary under NDA.

- Tombstone timeline (hosted):
  * Runtime cache eviction: immediate (seconds).
  * Request-level logs/payloads: deleted within 72 hours by default.
  * Backup/archive artifacts: standard hosted window 30 days; negotiable to 7/14/30 for Dedicated/Private with contractual terms.

- Keys & encryption: we support BYOK (bring-your-own-KMS). If Cedar provides their own KMS, Redwood never has access to plaintext KMS keys. Using customer KMS is the recommended path for additional assurance.

Next steps: if this aligns, I can (1) share the evidence bundle link for procurement, (2) run a short 30-minute call with your security team to walk the map, or (3) prepare contract language to pin region and reduce backup windows. Which would you prefer?

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
